n458b1375038.s: The Nellore Zamindari Rythu Sangham first met on 19 October 1929 at the house of:
n458b1375038.x: The Nellore Sangham first met at Dodla Ramireddy's house; Bhupathiraju Venkatapathiraju was President of the Andhra Rashtra Zamindari Rythu Sangham.

ndef76de368a.s: In the Challapalli zamindari struggle, the firing over Kishkindapalem land that killed four persons took place in:
ndef76de368a.x: The Kishkindapalem firing was in 1946, after the temple land grab (1939) and Rajeswara Rao and Chapanayya's leadership (1942), and before the July 1947 land occupation.

new.s: Who wrote 'Veera Telangana – Naa Anubhavalu, Gnapakalu'?
new.x: Veera Telangana is the memoir of Ravi Narayana Reddy; it is not by Mallu Swarajyam.

new.s: Chakali Ailamma, a symbol of the Telangana armed struggle, defended her land against the deshmukh of:
new.x: Chakali Ailamma, a washerwoman of Palakurthi, defended her land against the Visnur deshmukh.

new.s: 'Telangana People's Struggle and its Lessons' was written by:
new.x: P. Sundarayya wrote Telangana People's Struggle and its Lessons.

new.s: The 11th session of the Andhra Mahasabha (May 1944), fully dominated by communists, was held at:
new.x: The 11th session at Bhongir in May 1944 was fully dominated by communists; Chilkur hosted the 8th session (1941).

new.s: The Ryot Agitation of Andhra in 1933 was led by:
new.x: Parvataneni Veeriah Chowdary led the 1933 Ryot Agitation of Andhra.

new.s: The Rajakeeya Pathashala founded by N.G. Ranga in 1939 was located at:
new.x: Ranga founded the Rajakeeya Pathashala at Kankipadu in 1939; Nidubrolu had the first Kisan School (1933-34).

new.s: Ponaka Kanakamma backed the Zamindari Rytu movement of which district?
new.x: Ponaka Kanakamma was a woman activist of Nellore who backed the Zamindari Rytu movement there.

new.s: The Telugu weekly 'Zamin Rytu' (Nellore, 1930) was started by:
new.x: Zamin Rytu was started by Nellore Venkatarama Naidu as the voice of the Zamin Rytu movement.

new.s: The film 'Rythu Bidda', which dramatised the anti-zamindari issue, was made by:
new.x: Rythu Bidda was made by Gudavalli Ramabrahmam.

new.s: 'Nil Darpan', written by Dinabandhu Mitra, was published by:
new.x: Rev. James Long published Nil Darpan; Michael Madhusudan Dutt translated it.

new.s: The Indigo Revolt of 1859-60 was centred in which district of Bengal?
new.x: The Indigo Revolt was centred in Nadia, Bengal, under Digambar and Bishnu Biswas.

new.s: Who led the Indigo Revolt of 1859-60?
o: Ishan Chandra Roy and Shambhu Pal
Sitaram Das and Vijay Singh Pathik
Gauri Shankar Mishra and Indra Narayan Dwivedi
new.x: Digambar and Bishnu Biswas led the Indigo Revolt; Ishan Chandra Roy and Shambhu Pal led the Pabna Agrarian League.

new.s: The Pabna movement (1873-76) was directed against:
new.x: Pabna was a legal, peaceful protest against rent hikes by zamindars, not against indigo.

new.s: The Pabna movement led to the enactment of the:
new.x: The Pabna Agrarian League's struggle led to the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885.

new.s: The Deccan Riots of 1875 were mainly directed against:
new.x: Peasants of Poona and Ahmednagar attacked moneylenders' houses and burned debt bonds.

new.s: Which law, letting moneylenders seize peasants' land, was a cause of the Deccan Riots?
new.x: The Limitation Law of 1859 let moneylenders seize land, leading to the 1875 riots.

new.s: The Deccan Riots of 1875 broke out in:
new.x: The Deccan Riots occurred in Poona and Ahmednagar (Maharashtra), under ryotwari.

new.s: The Bijolia peasant movement (1897-1927) took place in:
new.x: Bijolia was in Mewar (Rajasthan), led by Sitaram Das and Vijay Singh Pathik.

new.s: The Sanyasi Revolt (1763-1800) broke out in Bengal after the famine of:
new.x: The Sanyasi Revolt followed the 1770 famine and curbs on pilgrimages.

new.s: Which of the following movements is NOT correctly matched with its region?
new.x: The Telangana armed struggle was in Hyderabad State; Malabar was the region of the Moplah revolt.

new.s: The All India Kisan Sabha was founded in April 1936 at the Congress session of:
new.x: AIKS was founded in April 1936 at the Lucknow session of the Congress.

new.s: Who was the first general secretary of the All India Kisan Sabha?
new.x: N.G. Ranga was general secretary; Sahajanand Saraswati was the first president.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the All India Kisan Sabha:
1. Its Kisan Manifesto of August 1936 demanded abolition of zamindari.
2. It adopted the red flag in October 1937.
3. Sahajanand Saraswati formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha after the AIKS was founded.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The manifesto (Aug 1936) and red flag (Oct 1937) are correct; Sahajanand formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha earlier, in 1929.

new.s: The Tebhaga demand to cut the landlord's share to one-third had been recommended by the:
new.x: The Floud Commission had recommended cutting the landlord's share from one-half to one-third.

new.s: Which legislation was an outcome of the Tebhaga movement?
new.x: The Tebhaga movement led to the Bargadari Act (1950).

new.s: In the Tebhaga movement, the bargadars struggled against the:
new.x: Bargadars (sharecroppers) fought the jotedars, the rich landholders of Bengal.

new.s: In the Moplah revolt of 1921, the Muslim tenants rose against Hindu landlords known as:
new.x: The Moplahs rose against the Hindu landlords (jenmis) and the British.

new.s: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was against a land revenue hike of:
new.x: Bardoli opposed a 30% hike in land revenue; Eka was about rent 50% above the recorded rent.

new.s: Vallabhbhai Patel earned the title 'Sardar' during the:
new.x: Patel got the title 'Sardar' during the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928.

new.s: The Eka Movement began among the farmers of which region?
new.x: Eka began among farmers of Hardoi, Bahraich and Sitapur in UP.

new.s: In the Oudh Kisan Sabha's grievances, the term 'begar' meant:
new.x: Begar was the forced labour exacted by the taluqdars of Oudh.

new.s: In the Telangana armed struggle, 'village soviets' were:
o: Cultural units of the early Andhra Mahasabha
Peasant committees set up after land redistribution
new.x: Village soviets were peasant committees set up in Telangana after land was redistributed.

new.s: In the Tebhaga movement, 'bargadars' or 'adhiars' were:
new.x: Bargadars or adhiars were sharecroppers; jotedars were rich landholders.

new.s: Which phase of peasant movements included Champaran (1917), Kheda (1918) and Bardoli (1928)?
new.x: These three belonged to the second phase, Gandhian satyagraha.

new.s: Under the zamindari system in Andhra, 'Pullari' was a:
new.x: Pullari was a grazing tax; Nazarana was the renewal fee.

new.s: The annual renewal fee for tenancy charged by zamindars was called:
new.x: Nazarana was the renewal fee; Bedalli meant eviction for non-payment.

new.s: Which of the following zamindari terms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
o: Kancha paddhati – Grazing land auctioned yearly
new.x: Bedalli meant eviction for non-payment; the grazing tax was Pullari.

new.s: In Madras Presidency, about what share of zamindari land lay in the Andhra districts?
new.x: About 70% of the Presidency's zamindari land lay in Andhra districts; 40% is Andhra's land under zamindars at Independence.

new.s: The Madras Estates Land Act, 1908:
o: Regulated landholder-ryot relations without abolishing estates
Gave all tenants ownership of land
new.x: The 1908 Act regulated tenancy; it did not abolish estates.

new.s: The Third Amendment (1936) to the Madras Estates Land Act gave occupancy rights to those in direct possession on:
new.x: The 1936 Third Amendment gave occupancy rights to those in direct possession on 30 June 1934; it came into force on 31 October 1936.

new.s: The 1934 Amendment (Madras Act VIII) to the Estates Land Act replaced 'an occupancy ryot' with:
new.x: The 1934 Amendment substituted section 8, replacing 'an occupancy ryot' by 'a ryot'.

new.s: The paper 'Prajavani', started by the first Zamindar Rythu Sabha of North Andhra, was edited by:
new.x: Prajavani (Vizag) was edited by Garimella Krishnamurthy; Zamin Ryot was Nellore Venkataramana Naidu's paper.

new.s: The first anti-zamindari conference, held at Venkatagiri in September 1931, was presided over by:
new.x: N.G. Ranga presided over the first anti-zamindari conference at Venkatagiri (Sept 1931).

new.s: The Mandasa police firing that killed five persons, including Pusumanu Gunnamma, took place in:
new.x: The Mandasa firing was on 1 April 1940 in Srikakulam; Palemkota was 1933.

new.s: The Bobbili agitation of 1922 against unfair land tax was led by:
new.x: Simhadri Suryanarayana led the Bobbili agitation of 1922.

new.s: In the Munagala estate, the harvest wage per acre was cut from 80 seers to:
new.x: The Munagala zamindar cut the wage from 80 to 60 seers per acre.

new.s: Who led the anti-zamindari struggle in Kalipatnam?
new.x: Bhupathiraju Lakshmi Narasimha Raju led Kalipatnam; Venkatapathiraju was President of the Andhra Rashtra Zamindari Rythu Sangham.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Yakasiri Chellamma led women's chilli-powder resistance in Nellore / Venkatagiri; Simhadri Suryanarayana led Bobbili and Gouthu Latchanna led the Ichchapuram yatra.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948:
1. It abolished both zamindari and inamdari estates.
2. Zamindars received no compensation under it.
3. It came into force on 7 September 1949.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Act abolished zamindari and inamdari estates and came into force on 7 September 1949; zamindars were compensated, so 2 is wrong.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Munagala paragana struggle:
1. Munagala was then in Nandigama taluk of Krishna district.
2. The agitation was withdrawn on 19 June 1939 after Prakasam and Ranga promised action.
3. The Brahmaiah Award covered 124 villages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Munagala was in Nandigama taluk, Krishna, and the agitation was withdrawn on 19 June 1939; the Brahmaiah Award covered 142 villages, not 124.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the All India Kisan Sabha?
o: It was first named the All India Kisan Congress
It was founded at Palasa in 1940
new.x: AIKS was founded in April 1936 at Lucknow; Palasa hosted a session in March 1940.

new.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Telangana armed struggle is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Ravi Narayana Reddy – 8th Andhra Mahasabha, Chilkur
Mallu Swarajyam – Author of Veera Telangana
new.x: Veera Telangana was written by Ravi Narayana Reddy, not Mallu Swarajyam; the other pairs are correct.

new.s: The Prakasam Committee on the zamindari system completed its report on:
new.x: The report was completed on 7 November 1938; the Abolition Bill came on 11 November 1947.

new.s: When the zamindari committee was appointed in 1937, T. Prakasam held the post of:
new.x: Prakasam was Revenue Minister in Rajaji's ministry when the committee was set up in 1937.

new.s: The Madras Estates Abolition Act received the assent of Governor-General C. Rajagopalachari on:
new.x: Assent came on 2 April 1949; it came into force on 7 September 1949.

new.s: The Krishna District Rythu Sangham, an early peasant body in Andhra, was formed in:
new.x: The Krishna District Rythu Sangham was formed in 1915; Guntur and Godavari sanghams came in 1923.

new.s: The demands of the Kisan movement in Andhra included MSP, minimum wages and:
new.x: The Kisan movement demanded MSP, minimum wages and zamindari abolition.

new.s: Which Andhra kisan leader was called 'Rythu Pedda'?
new.x: Gottipati Brahmaiah was called 'Rythu Pedda'; Ranga was 'Rythu Bandhu'.

new.s: Who is called the 'Father of the Indian Peasant Movement'?
new.x: N.G. Ranga is known as the Father of the Indian Peasant Movement and Rythu Bandhu.

new.s: N.G. Ranga founded the Rajakeeya Pathashala at Kankipadu in:
new.x: The Rajakeeya Pathashala at Kankipadu dates from 1939; the Nidubrolu school from 1933-34.

new.s: The Indian Peasants Institute founded by N.G. Ranga was located at:
new.x: The Indian Peasants Institute (first Kisan School) was at Nidubrolu, Guntur, in 1933-34.

new.s: Which of the following were journals of N.G. Ranga?
o: Credo of World Peasantry and Fight for Freedom
new.x: Praja Bandhu and Navayuga were Ranga's journals; Credo of World Peasantry and Fight for Freedom are his books.

new.s: The 1933 Ryot agitation of Andhra was led by:
new.x: Parvataneni Veeriah Chowdary led the 1933 Ryot agitation.

new.s: The Guntur anti-resettlement movement of 1935 was led by:
new.x: N.G. Ranga led the 1935 Guntur anti-resettlement movement.

new.s: The 1931 no-tax resolution of the Divi taluk Resettlement Mahasabha was passed at:
new.x: The Divi taluk Resettlement Mahasabha met at Mopidevi in 1931 under Gottipati Brahmaiah.

new.s: The Palasa session of the All India Kisan Sabha, presided by Sahajanand, was held in:
new.x: The Palasa AIKS session was in March 1940; Ranga was jailed for defying his confinement.

new.s: Before his death in 1950, Sahajanand Saraswati formed the All India United Kisan Sabha, which demanded:
new.x: The All India United Kisan Sabha demanded nationalisation of land and waterways.

new.s: The Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra was launched by N.G. Ranga on:
new.x: Ranga launched the yatra on 3 July 1937.

new.s: Who led the 1937 Rythu Rakshana Yatra on the ground?
new.x: Ranga launched the yatra, but Kommareddi Satyanarayana led it on the ground.

new.s: The Brahmaiah Award of 15 January 1939 in the Munagala struggle covered how many villages?
new.x: The Brahmaiah Award (15 Jan 1939) was a settlement covering 142 villages.

new.s: 'Munagala Day' was observed on:
new.x: Munagala Day was 11 June 1939; the agitation was withdrawn on 19 June 1939.

new.s: The June 1930 revolt of Potharlanka, Ghantasala and Movva farmers in the Challapalli struggle was led by:
new.x: Gorrepati Venkata Subbayya led the June 1930 revolt; Rajeswara Rao and Chapanayya led in 1942.

new.s: In 1939, the Challapalli zamindar grabbed how many acres of temple land?
new.x: The zamindar grabbed 600 acres of temple land in 1939.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a founder of the Andhra Provincial Ryots Association (1928)?
new.x: Ranga, Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana and Maganti Bapineedu founded it; B.V. Ratnam was its first General Secretary.

new.s: The Andhra Provincial Ryots Association merged into the All India Kisan Sabha in:
new.x: It merged into AIKS in 1936.
